
# LAB:Unprotected Admin Functionality

__Path Traversal__
Path traversal also known as Directory Traversal vulnerabilities enable an attacker to interact with arbitrary files on a server,giving them access to sensitive data.If they can potentially modify an application data or behaviour ultimately taking full control of the server

### LAb:Unprotected Admin Functionality
![Server-Side-Vulnerabilities 20260812-100903.png|523](data:image/png;base64,)

To solve this lab I tried some path traversing to the admin panel by appending the */admin*
to the link but did not work then I decide use some metadata files used by web-crawlers on navigating a domain
For this catse I use the  __robots.txt__ file and got the page below.

![Server-Side-Vulnerabilities 20260812-102255.png](data:image/png;base64,)

The robots.txt file revealed the name of the admin panel used on this page so I appended the exact name instead ofguessing and see what it reavels

### Take aways:
This lab demonstrates how a server fails to enforce authorization

### key notes~
To prevent such vulnerability the developer/server  should implement:
- Authenticate the user
- Verify the user's role and the permissions the user has on the server
- Deny unauthorized request with 401/403 
- Apply authorization checks to every priviledged endpoint/action
- Do not treat the web-server metadata files i.e robots.txt,sitemap.xml or obscurity as a security mechanism
```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /administrator-panel
```

From the above demo: the web-crawler was directed not to navigate the admin panel which probably worked but reveled it in the process
